built.name: epic-build-change-doc
built.blurb: Build change documentation the way a good analyst writes it: what changed, which records were touched, who feels it in the workflow, how it was validated, and how you roll it back at 2am when it breaks.

built.name: clinical-workflow-analysis
built.blurb: A current-state and future-state workflow analysis with the evidence labeled (observed, reported, documented, or assumed), a pain-point table, a root-cause pass, and a measurement plan.

built.name: request-triage
built.blurb: Routes a pasted ticket, email, or chat ask through three tests in order: break/fix, net new, enhancement, or optimization. Then the track, the domain, the scope, and a ready-to-paste ticket with the lead, the executor, and the approver named. The standard is this site's request-routing module.

built.name: data-request-spec
built.blurb: Turns "can you pull me a list of..." into a spec two analysts would build the same way: population, grain, time window, a definitions table with every filter's source labeled, minimum-necessary fields, and a validation plan the requester can run.

built.name: cds-alert-review
built.blurb: A design review for a BPA or any interruptive alert: trigger logic with each element labeled, audience, format, the actions offered, expected volume from a silent run, coded override reasons, retirement criteria, and a measurement plan. Alert fatigue, with the numbers.

entries.name: anthropics/skills
entries.whatItIs: Anthropic's own skills repository: example skills across creative, technical, enterprise, and document work, plus the Agent Skills specification and a starter template.
entries.whyYouCare: This is the reference implementation. The docx, pdf, pptx, and xlsx skills behind Claude's document features live here as source-available code. If you want to see what a production skill looks like, this is it.
entries.stealThis: The /template folder. Copy it, rename it, and you have a valid skill scaffold in about thirty seconds.

entries.name: Agent Skills spec (agentskills.io)
entries.whatItIs: The vendor-neutral standard behind SKILL.md files. Skills written to this spec work in Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, and most other agent tooling.
entries.whyYouCare: Portability. A skill you write for your team isn't locked to one vendor's product. In a health system that just went through a vendor consolidation cycle, that matters.
entries.stealThis: The frontmatter rules. Name plus description is the entire triggering mechanism, and the spec explains why.

entries.name: obra/superpowers
entries.whatItIs: The dominant community framework. Working skills for test-driven development, debugging, planning, and collaboration, plus commands like /brainstorm and /write-plan. North of 280,000 stars as of September 2026.
entries.whyYouCare: An opinionated methodology for how an agent should work through a complex task, packaged as skills. Worth studying even if you never install it.
entries.stealThis: The planning-before-execution discipline. It maps cleanly onto how a good analyst approaches an Epic build.

entries.name: karanb192/awesome-claude-skills
entries.whatItIs: A verified, maintained list of 50-plus skills covering TDD, debugging, git workflows, and document processing. One of several overlapping awesome-lists; this one prioritizes verification.
entries.whyYouCare: When you want to know what exists without wading through the noise, start here.
entries.stealThis: Nothing directly. Use it to find out what exists, then read the actual skill before you install anything.

entries.name: skills.sh and mcp.directory
entries.whatItIs: The app-store layer. Browse skills by category, install with one command, track versions. skills.sh is skills only; mcp.directory indexes MCP servers and skills side by side, more than nine thousand skills at last count.
entries.whyYouCare: Discovery. Also a preview of where this is heading: skills as installable, versioned units instead of prompt snippets pasted from a wiki.
entries.stealThis: The one-command install pattern, if you ever distribute skills to your own team.

entries.name: anthropics/claude-for-legal
entries.whatItIs: Anthropic's official plugin suite for legal teams: drafting, review, and search workflows.
entries.whyYouCare: Anthropic is building profession-specific plugin packs. Healthcare is an obvious next vertical, and right now the practitioner side of that territory is unclaimed.
entries.stealThis: The framing. A vertical skill pack is deep workflow knowledge written down. Clinical informatics has that knowledge in abundance and almost none of it written in this format.
